 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.112 of 2018 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-II, Thalassery, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 10/01/2020.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-II, Thalassery
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The sole respondent herein is the 3rd respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 15/09/2017 at about 01:45 p.m., while he was pillion riding on motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-58-R-6912 from Mahe to Thalassery and when he reached the place by name Kidaram Kunnu, autorickshaw bearing registration no.KL-56-R-76, driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked him down, as a result of which he 2025:KER:74231 sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/owner remained ex parte.
4. The second respondent/driver did not file written statement.
5. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending autorickshaw.
The age, occupation and income were disputed.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A8 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No evidence was produced by the respondents.
Ext.X1 disability certificate was also marked.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending autorickshaw resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 4,48,500/- together with interest @ 8%
per annum from the date of petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.

sentences.text: The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a salesman, was earning 20,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 8,500/- which is quite low and hence, the same needs to be appropriately enhanced.
She relies on Exts.A7 and A8 in support of the argument regarding income.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the amount fixed is reasonable and if at all the Court is inclined to enhance the same, it may be as per the dictum in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal was not inclined to rely on Exts.A7 and A8 as the person who issued the same was not examined.
It is submitted 2025:KER:74231 by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that when the marking of the document was not objected to, the Tribunal was not justified in not relying on the same.

It is well settled that mere marking of a document is not proof of contents of the same (Sait Tarajee Khimchand v. Yelamarti Satyam Alias Satteyya, AIR 1971 SC 1865; Ramji Dayawala &
Sons (P) Ltd v. Invest Import, AIR 1981 SC 2085).

entities.text: Sait Tarajee Khimchand v. Yelamarti Satyam Alias Satteyya, AIR 1971 SC 1865
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, I do not find any infirmity committed by the Tribunal in not relying on Exts.A7 and A8 when the contents of the same was not proved.
However, going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the income of the claim petitioner can be fixed as 11,000/-.
Loss of earnings 10.
The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained injury of fracture of left femoral condyle.
He was hospitalized for a period of 27 days.
In all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 7 months.
Hence, he can be awarded compensation at the rate of 11,000/-x7 months = 77,000/-.
Percentage of disability 11.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that going by Ext.X1 disability certificate, the disability has 2025:KER:74231 been fixed as 45% and so Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the disability to 15%.

Hence, she submits that since the claim petitioner is a salesman,
the injury caused has caused difficulties which are referred to in Ext.X1 which would certainly affect his functioning or his efficiency in discharge of his duties and therefore, the Tribunal ought not to have reduced the percentage of the functional disability.
11.1. Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the percentage of disability that is shown in Ext.X1 is locomotor disability.
The Tribunal has taken the whole body disability as 15% and therefore, there is no infirmity calling for an interference by this Court.
11.2. Exhibit X1 disability certificate reads thus.

sentences.text: We, the Chairman and Members of the Medical Board, General Hospital, Thalassery constituted on 18.09.2019 have this day examined Sri/Smt MOHAMMED AFSAL s/o HAMEED, DARUL HAMD (H) KOTTAYAMPOYIL P.O. and found that he/she is suffering from fracture of left, medial femoral condyle following an RTA sustained on 15/09/17.

He has got post traumatic stiffness of left hip,
knee and ankle.
We are the opinion that he has got 45% (forty five percentage) total permanent locomotor disability in relation to the left lower limb."
The fact that he is a salesman is not seen disputed and therefore, the difficulty caused to a certain extent would effect his functioning as a salesman.

Hence, I find that the functional disability can be fixed as 20%.

2,42,703/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
